text:
Maxim Shabanov came out of the KHL undrafted, spent last season on Long Island scoring five goals in 44 games, and has become a power-play weapon in Minnesota. He has 8 goals and 13 points in 18 games, nine on the power play, and scored three times in two nights against San Jose and Tampa Bay. Our breakout flag likes it: his ice time is up to 15:06 a night from 13:41, and he is on the ice for 73% of his team's power-play chances, up from 27%.

The role is the real part. His own chances are up to 0.85 expected goals per 60 from 0.62 (expected goals measure the quality of chances). The shooting is the part to doubt: 8 goals on 3.9 expected, a 29% shooting rate against 9% last season.

The worry is at even strength. With him on the ice at 5v5, the Wild get only 45.9% of the expected goals, 9.6 points worse than the team without him. That is a power-play specialist's profile for now. We'd expect his goal pace to cool but the power-play minutes to keep the points coming.
headline: Shabanov's breakout is real, the finishing less so
